incident_description:
On 6/29/2024 at approximately 6:50pm EST (later confirmed by video to be at [REDACTED] as per surveillance video), I was putting away an empty shopping cart at the Harris Teeter store located at [REDACTED] when the wheels locked up and an alarm went off. This abrupt locking of the wheels caused a jarring stop (as clearly shown in the video) which injured me. The device involved in the locking of the cart wheel is the PurChek System.

Initially, I dismissed the incident as a mere part of modern life but as the evening went on I began to experience back pain, shooting sensations, pins and needles and numbness in my legs, prompting a visit to urgent care the next day (6/30/2024). Further issues with numbness and pain prompted me to go to a second urgent care visit on 7/5/2024. I recently visited a spine specialist (8/19/2024) who confirmed that my continuing symptoms are tied to the incident and prescribed physical therapy. While I am for the most part recovered, I still have unresolved back pain which I hope the physical therapy will address.

Out of a concern for public safety, I reached out to Harris Teeter, who refused to engage with my concerns except to state the device was operating as intended when it injured me. In the process of dialogue with their Third Party Claims Adjuster (TPA), [REDACTED], I was informed that injuries of my nature were not uncommon from the intake person I talked to.

Seeing as Harris Teeter and its representative were not responsive to my concerns and they involved a risk to the public, I reached out to the North Carolina Attorney Generals Office (AG). While Harris Teeter was initially non-responsive to the AG, they finally responded after the AG reached out a second time but merely provided statements that the device carries no risk while stating they can acquire safety information to support such a claim if necessary while simultaneously attacking and ignoring my concerns.  

I held off on reporting this incident to the CPSC until such time as I had confirmation of the product involved in my injury (which was included in the Harris Teeter response to the AG). I have confirmed that the device in question has been reported previously and the report number is [REDACTED]..

I'm attaching the following:
1. The response of Harris Teeter to the AG, 
2. The notes on my calculations of the forces involved, 
3. Relevant medical records illustrating the extent of my injuries, 
4. Video of the incident, 
5. Photos of the shopping cart notices, 
6. The brochure associated with the device which injured me
7. News reports indicating a broader pattern of injury
8. A copy of my complaint to the AG

Overall,
My concerns, as relevant to the CPSC, boil down the following:
1.This device has a strong risk of injury, in particular injury for certain vulnerable populations (i.e. the elderly, the young, those who are pregnant, and those with pre-existing health issues or disabilities). 
2. This device does not seem to carry any safety information associated with it (certainly, none was shared with those who purchased the device since they would to will consider obtaining that information if requested)
3. The extent of risk mitigations is that the carts contain a sign saying Shopping Carts may stop unexpectedly at exit doors. In the absence of a statement indicating that in doing so it may injure, that is not a sufficient safety warning.

My request is that the CPSC conducts a full investigation into the safety of the PurChek System to assess the risks to the consumers. A good starting point for that might be the following:
1. Reaching out to Harris Teeter and their representative to confirm the incident I experienced (the Store Manager is one [REDACTED], the attorney who responded to the AG in this matter is one [REDACTED], and one [REDACTED] with their Third Party Claims Adjuster (TPA), [REDACTED]). By doing so, CPSC can more clearly document the incident and acquire additional information 
2. Requesting records associated with this and other incidents from Harris Teeter and their TPA, [REDACTED]. By doing so, CPSC can begin to establish a pattern of injury and risk associated with this product. 
3. Requesting safety information from the manufacturer on the PurChek System (if such safety information exists) to determine the degree of risk to consumers.

Please know, I am fully at the disposal of your office should it prove necessary. The oft-stated idea that safety regulations are written in blood is one I would like us to avoid this time. Don't hesitate if there is any additional information I could provide.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, with symptoms persisting over a month and requiring medical intervention, indicating a likely occurrence with significant impact.

To whom it may concern: 
I am writing this letter in regards to a recent finding about my Waupaca elevator, (serial number qualifies), of 17 plus years. By sheer accident I learned that this elevator has had a recall. I was shocked to hear of this, particularly, because I never received such a notice of a recall. I am 77 years of age and have become VERY dependent on an elevator in a three story home. The risk of a free fall, as I was told was one of the problems, makes use of the elevator a risk, and not one that I want myself or family to take. 
After going back and forth with a couple of elevator maintenance companies, one of which I have had servicing my elevator for many years, I was given your address as a possible source of help in addressing what follows. 
I have been told that the elevator recall makes having any needed repairs not legally possible until it is either upgraded or to have a new elevator installed. The upgrade, as of date, would cost $17,000 and a brand new elevator, as of date, would cost $30,000.
Apparently, the Waupaca manufacturer assets were sold through a receivership proceeding to Wisconsin Elevator Company, LLC d/b/a Fox Valley Elevator. At this time, there is no remedy available for consumers with Waupaca elevators. My question is, why should I be expected to pay for the recall of my elevator particularly considering the high cost of repair or replacement and ,most important, it's not my fault or responsibility. I find this situation unacceptable. I have several neighbors that have the same elevator, and they are hoping I can find some information or course of action that can be taken. 
And therein is the reason for this letter. Can you please help me with this situation?? 
I would greatly appreciate hearing back from you. My home is in [REDACTED], Delaware for your information. I will be happy to provide more information if needed, and to work with you to find a remedy to this problem.
Thank you in advance for any and all help you can share with me. I look forward to hearing back from you in the not too distant future.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
On Saturday, August 20, 2022 around 3pm, I entered a Kroger to refill plastic 5-gallon jugs with water at the Glacier water refill station on aisle 11.  These jugs had water in them the week before and were used to holding water.  The first jug filled up with five gallons just fine.  The water stopped after each gallon, and I had to press the start button after what looked like a gallon (5x). As the second jug was filling up almost to the top, I looked over at my cart and then turned back to push the off button, when I heard a loud boom and saw that the bottom of the jug had exploded outward toward me. Both of my hands and wrists were impacted, and I held my left wrist with my right hand because it was bleeding and in a lot of pain.  Water was all over the floor and the jug was missing its bottom. The Kroger shift manager [REDACTED] and the security staff helped keep customers away from me while my partner tried to calm me down and make sure I had all my fingers. The staff brought me some ice, and I spoke with [REDACTED] the pharmacist who said he used to work in the ER and thought if I was able to hold my wrist the way that I was that the wrist was not broken.  We left the store and went to urgent care after giving our names and numbers to [REDACTED] and his boss [REDACTED].  Xrays showed that I did not have any broken bones, but had serious soft tissue contusions and sprains. I will be out of work for the next two weeks at least. I returned to the same Kroger on Monday, August 22, 2022 and the Glacier station was not marked as ÃÂOut of OrderÃÂ or anything, even though the blue top pour spout was missing on the unit that was present on Saturday.  I wanted to report this so the machine gets checked  and no one else gets hurt. Thank you for anything you can see to do.

The machine in this report had www.glacierwater.com on the side -- that site appears to no longer exist. I believe Primo operates most Glacier sites now: https://primowater.com/self-service-refill-water/

incident_description: Early April 2021, I purchased an LED neon sign from Yellow Pop USA.  hello@yellowpop.com . I found the general quality of the product poor (made in China) and the electrical power component supplied potentially dangerous to children, adults and pets. My concern about the safety issue was presented to two individuals at Yellow Pop and brought no results. I was told by both individuals (I have emails) that my issue of high voltage electrocution is of no concern as the LED power supply is "low voltage".  Well the 120 volt AC power cord terminals (directly from the wall outlet) are completely exposed and the owners manual for the power supply (online power supply manufacturer) states specifically under "Hazards" that the component is to be mounted in an enclosure. Obviously the power supply manufacture understands this high voltage unit is to be shielded to avoid an electrocution hazard. Yellow pop scoffs at the concern and so far has refused restitution to me. I have photos of the power supply and a link to the power supply owners manual posted below. The power supply that came with the sign by Yellow Pop (to lay openly exposed on the floor or mount exposed on the wall) is a model LRS-150-12 at www.meanwell.com . The warning to shield this unit is on the Meanwell website. Since potentially thousands of these power supplies were supplied to U.S. customers for their LED signs, I believe this is a potential hazard that needs to be addressed due to the exposed high voltage wires creating a shock hazard. I emailed the Underwriters Laboratory May 7, 2021 and they informed me by telephone today, May 12, 2021 that this is a serious hazard issue and yes, that this power supply is designed to be covered and installed as part of a component. They also mentioned that my complaint is out of their jurisdiction however as the Yellow Pop product is not "UL Approved".  They recommended that I contact Saferproducts.gov.
justification: Exposed high voltage wires pose a significant shock hazard, especially for children and pets, making an injury likely.

incident_description:
In October of 2020, two unreported fires occurred in two separate solar powered street lights, professionally
installed within a mobile home park to illuminate their private streets.
Both fires involved the battery pack and connected electrical wiring, effectively destroying both units.
The first fire occurred during the day, presumably while the unit was charging. According to park maintenance the
fire self-extinguished and the only damage was scorching to the street and brick wall directly beneath the light
standard. The unit was disposed of by maintenance.
The second fire occurred in the evening while the light was illuminating. This fire started a small spot fire in the
vegetation below the light standard, and apparently involved an explosion of the battery pack as hot metal
shrapnel was found imbedded in a cloth patio furniture cushion approximately 20 feet away. No further fire
damage was found and no injuries were reported.
Photos of the second solar light were obtained and the unit itself was kept by the mobile home park HOA president.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the potential for property damage and future incidents is high.

7.29.20 4:PM Walgreens -8088 Antoine Dr. Houston, TX 77088 (281) 272-2592

Exited Walgreens with a double basket metal grocery cart.  Walked on their walkway past 3 parking lot stalls to my car.  I pushed the first two wheels of the basket over the curb since my vehicle was located about 1 foot away.  The first two wheels went over the curb but never touched the ground until the cart tipped over with me on top of it.  These grocery carts dimensions cause a hazard to consumers.  The distance between the front wheels and the back means the front wheels can not land safely on the ground without tipping over the whole cart.  

My injuries known so far-sprains, strains, back pain, wrist pain, leg and ankle pain, headache, nausea, head injury,arm and torso pain.
justification: Injuries sustained due to the unstable design of the grocery cart, which tipped over when attempting to cross the curb.

incident_description: My son attends a preschool in [REDACTED].  On Friday, January 10th at approximately 10:30 am, the kids were in the hall getting their snow clothes on to go outside.  My son and another little boy were trying to get my son's coat and snow pants off the hook of the lockers by pulling on them.  The cabinet then tipped over.  The other little boy was able to jump out of the way, but my son wasn't so lucky.  The entire 105 pound cabinet tipped over and he was completely trapped underneath.  The top of the cabinet hit the bridge of his nose and above his right eye.  Ambulances were called and he was transported to the nearest hospital.  He underwent a CT scan right away where they determined he broke his nose and needed surgery to set the bone and stitch him up.  The school had a thorough safety investigation with the State of [REDACTED] and it was determined there was no safety violation.  In fact, no licensed day care providers in [REDACTED] are required to anchor the cubbies to the wall.  The licensing investigator does agree that this is a manufacturing issue.  He is healing at this point, but he will have a scar on his nose and hopefully we will be able to address the scar tissue forming.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury (broken nose requiring surgery) to the child, and the likelihood of a similar incident occurring again is high due to the lack of anchoring requirements for cubbies in [REDACTED] daycare centers.

incident_description:
*MY ARM COULD HAVE BEEN CRUSHED OR SEVERED - THIS IS NO JOKE! *

Sat 6/22/19 ~10:00 AM CDT

Walmart in Fenton, MO 63026, is testing an unsafe package pickup tower made in Finland that CRUSHED MY PACKAGE and would not let it go. There was no safety release mechanism after I failed to remove the package during the 10 seconds or so it took to take these pix. I wedged the box, thinking the robotic door would retract - it didn't. Instead, the door kept trying to close, pushing down without raising up, crushing the package over and over while the display said, "Remove object blocking door." - with no way to do so.

*MY ARM COULD HAVE BEEN CRUSHED OR SEVERED - THIS IS NO JOKE! *

What if a curious child stuck a hand or a head inside (to see where the packages come from) and the door came down and caused decapitation?

No employees knew how to open the machine and no one was strong enough to lift the robotic door. The machine has no instructions on it and store personnel had not been trained on it.

Keep your children away from this dangerous device Walmart is testing nationwide that will also take away more human jobs. (Two Customer Service staffers were standing idle that Saturday morning with no customers to assist.)

Sat 6/22/19 1:30 PM CDT

Follow-up two hours after: A store manager phoned me to say that the robot's vendor came after I left the store and released the package. The contents had shifted away from the crushing door and were okay. He assured me that my package would be held at the Customer Service counter for me to pickup from a staffer after I refused to use the Package Tower. Walmart will give me a $10 gift card for my "inconvenience."

Mon 6/24/19 10:00 AM CDT 

Follow-up two days after this incident: Went to pick up my crushed package at the Fenton, MO Walmart Customer Service desk only to be informed by a female clerk that the computer indicated that it had been put back into the Package Tower even though I was told it would be held for me at the desk. I informed the manager there had been an incident with the robot and I would not use the Package Tower. The polite and professional clerk summoned a polite and professional female manager who went to retrieve my package while I waited at Customer Service. When she returned with the goods, I explained what happened, and she said it must have been a "glitch" in the Package Tower because whenever she reached her arm underneath the door, the door stopped (or retracted, I'm not sure which).

This "glitch" could quite easily maim or kill. This "glitch" allows a powerful robotic door to crush relentlessly downward with no safety release switch, no machine instructions, and no trained staff on a Saturday morning. It is mind-boggling that no Walmart employee shared my sense of concern. The vendor tech had cleared the box, presumably cleared the "glitch," and the robot was back in business making easy money for Walmart 24/7.

Worse, recent news articles from Walmart say they plan to install these dangerous and undertested devices in 700 stores nationwide by the end of 2019. Source: https://blog.walmart.com/innovation/20180405/hundreds-more-high-tech-pickup-towers-are-headed-your-way

A half hour later I left the Fenton, MO Walmart Customer Service desk with the contents of my package (the crushed box was nowhere to be seen) and a $10 gift card, as promised. I will never place an online order with any Walmart that routes me to a detective Package Tower.

Pass this WARNING to everyone you know and let Walmart it's not okay to present under-tested and unsafe "glitchy" equipment into the general public.
justification: The incident involved a near-miss injury, with the potential for severe harm, and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the lack of safety measures and trained staff.

incident_description: I stepped onto a escalator at the Manchester Boston Regional Airport leading up from the check in counter to the TSA  security check in.  I was wearing rugged soled hiking shoes and I stepped onto the center of the step.  The escalator was not busy with one family of three at least 10 steps behind me.  I actually looked down at the escalator to make sure that my feet were centered.  I was not walking on the escalator had only a small carry on bag with me.  Approximately 1/2 way up the escalator I felt a bump which shifted my footing slightly into the riser of the step in front of me.  I noticed that my shoe was caught and though that I could free it by pulling on it.  When the escalator reached the top, the tread and riser came together, pulling my shoe and foot into the space between the tread and riser.  When the escalator reached the top, the comb sheared the front two inches off of my rugged shoes and nipped off the top of three toes.  I threw my body weight forward and pulled my foot out of the shoe, causing further injury to my ankle and permanent disability to my knee.  The Escalator company maintained that there was no manufacturing defect on the device.  This accident is bothersome because I followed all the guidelines provided by CPSC Release number: 08-264 and they were not sufficient to prevent a permanent disability. This accident could have been devastating had a child's foot become entrapped, because they would not have the strength to pull their foot from a tied sturdy shoe.
justification: Injury occurred due to escalator design, despite following safety guidelines, and could have been catastrophic for a child.

incident_description: My two and a half year old was pushing her mini kids cart while shopping, going slowly and straight down the side of the canned food aisle at the grocery store. The kids cart have tall metal rods with a hard plastic flag attached to the top that says "customer in training" on it. This flag became wedged between the cans on the high shelf above her and as she pushed her cart forward, the flag dislodged a can which struck her on the top of her head, leaving her screaming in pain and with a large, purple, raised bruise from the impact. These heavy metal rods also make the cart very easy to tip because they are placed to one side of the cart and we have had them tip over onto our small child while trying to turn corners in the store. These flag poles attached to mini kids shopping carts are very dangerous.
justification: Injury occurred due to the cart's flag dislodging a can, striking the child's head, leaving a visible bruise.

incident_description:
Pertinent to recall 16-238 - Porta Elevators EMDL (Electro-magnetic Door Lock) failure.

We have had a hoistway door open when the elevator car is not at the floor (twice).  This results in a fall hazard in an open hoistway.

We have circa 2005 Generation #1 Plastic Door Locks.

The problem appears to be a Porta EMDL not properly engaging to hold the door shut.  In reviewing the recall it is difficult to tell whether our issue is pertinent to the plastic part of the latch or the overall mechanical function of the door lock.  Either way we have had a door come open twice when the car was not on the floor.  The behavior feels as though the latch was only partially engaged and when pulled it held for a moment and then released.

IMPORTANT NOTE:  We have an American Crescent Elevator that incorporates the Porta products including the EMDL's.  To my knowledge Porta does not manufacture elevators but products that are used in residential elevators.  It would seem like the actual elevators that incorporate the recalled product should be listed?
justification: Potential fall hazard exists due to door opening when elevator car is not at the floor, with two previous occurrences.

Significant damage to the plastic housing on the discharge end of the device was observed. justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused significant damage to the smoke machine and garage.

Fortunately, the girl's parents were able to force the hoistway door open and the girl's aunt was able to pull the girl out of the space before the elevator arrived, saving her from catastrophic injury or death just moments before the elevator arrived at the floor.

incident_description: I just recently became a residential customer of [REDACTED] a dispenser, and had a water cooler and several large five gallon glass containers of water delivered. Today I changed bottles for the first time as we used up the full first jug. As a first time user I was not aware that when I peeled back the white tab covering the center of the neck of the bottle and turned it over to put it on the cooler it would not easily slide through the center. Rather what happens is that it rests momentarily with the full weight of the water and bottle on the plastic center until that breaks away and the bottle drops into the dispenser. Unfortunately if you are not aware of this sudden drop of the water then you don't know that it will not ease down but rather drops forcefully. My pinky happened to be near the neck of the bottle at a pinch point and as the full weight dropped the force smashed my pinky and shattered the bone. This is a ridiculously dangerous design which should be corrected immediately and significant warnings should be in place for customers to be made aware. I'm in tremendous pain and my fingertip is shattered.
justification: The design flaw in the water bottle, combined with user inexperience, led to a severe injury.

incident_description: Innowave Model 12-CHCMU3 filtered water dispenser. The dispenser has a UV lamp in it to assist in the water cleaning process. This lamp needs periodic replacement. This NVI Advanced Dispensing System - an electronic paper towel dispenser mounted on the public bathroom wall of a local grocery store poses a large threat to users, due to it's exposed sawtooth, razor sharp cutters. (see Photos) I am an example of a consumer who experienced an exceedingly painful 1/2" long and 3/8" wide deep furrow carved on the inside of my index finger in the middle section. (please see photo taken 2/12/14 the day-after. In it the flap of skin Is sitting in the furrow of my finger in hopes it will reunite.) (Also a 3 week later finger photo).

This incident occurred while reaching for the paper towel, my finger was impaled by the sawtooth blade and when I withdrew my hand it ripped out a large piece of flesh, hanging by one end. There was enormous pain, a lot of blood. (AFTER my incident) the store put a warning sign on the dispenser (see photo.) The new sign Is not a deterrent for many people, certainly not small children or the illiterate.

Most public paper towel dispensers have a very pronounced series of bends the paper comes through -to COVER the cutting blade and prevent injuries such as mine. This product should have one as well.
In my opinion this dispenser is unsafe and a hazard. It should be modified or removed before other injuries occur.
justification: The exposed, razor-sharp cutters caused a deep, painful injury, with the potential for more incidents given the lack of deterrent warning.

incident_description:
Koala Kare Child Protection Seat. Mom put 3 year old child into seat in restroom @ Dairy Queen and seat collapsed. Child fell onto tile floor.
Asst. manager said this has happened before. Dairy Queen continued to keep this seat in restroom.

On August 14, 2013 I took my daughter and my two grandchildren to the Dairy Queen Located at [REDACTED] for dinner. My daughter took her five year old daughter and three year old son to use the restroom while I prepared the table and waited for our food.

I heard loud cries coming from the restroom as did the employees as there were two employees sitting at a nearby table. I ran into the restroom and was told by my daughter that she placed her 3 year old son in the seat the Koala Wall Seat. Then the seat itself collapsed sending him to the floor. It was a hard fall unto the tile floor. He was obviously hurt by hitting the floor. After we were able to the console him we went out to our booth. On the way to the booth I asked the employee sitting nearby to please find a manager for us. A young woman came to our booth. I asked for an incident report so I could report what had just occurred. Her response was if an incident report was given we would have to take the child to the ER. We were not given an incident report.
I as my grandson's grandmother should have insisted on filing out an incident report. She also stated that his has happened before. We were then offered ice cream for the children (which we had already paid for). Ad I was leaving I went in to check to make sure that some measure had been taken to block off the seat so that it was unusable there was no tape of signage to indicate that the seat was broken. I called today and spoke to 
[REDACTED] (store manager) and asked if he was in fact present last evening when the incident happened. He said he was. He also stated that he had told the actual owner of the facility of the incident and that he was going to replace the seat. He also stated that the seat said for infants only. It did not. I took a photo of the seat and there is no signage of any weight limit or age limit. My grandson is 3 years old and weights 36 lbs. When I looked of the Koala Kare websight it lists the weight limit as 50 lbs. When I take my grandchildren out to dinner I have an expectation that they will be safe. And that all equipment intended for children will function properly. How many other children could be harmed by this seat. If the facility was aware that other children had been hurt when the seat collapsed why wasn't it removed or replace? This special evening that I had planned for my grandchildren was ruined because of someone's negligence in having a faulty seat in the restroom.
I will like assurance that this matter will be rectified so that no other child will be injured while in Dairy Queen.
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a child, and the likelihood of a recurrence is high given the store's history and lack of action.

incident_description:
The consumer reported that Sparkletts the water delivery service owned by DS Waters of America provided him with a water dispenser which flooded his home because of faulty parts. The top portion of the Atlantis Cooler [made by Oasis International, owned by Patriarch Partners, rented to consumers by Sparkletts which is owned by DS Waters of America, in turn owned by Kelso & Company], would detach itself from the cooler body with every bottle change.  At the time of this happening during the bottle change, I wasn't aware of the rubber gasket's purpose resulting in me putting the piece back onto the cooler the wrong way.

When the flood happened the rubber gasket was not seated properly and caused the cooler's internal water reservoir to overflow onto the floor.  Not being a water cooler design engineer, I wasn't aware of the piece was supposed to be put back on the water cooler each time I changed the 5 gallon bottles.  I complained to Sparkletts about this piece coming off each time I changed the bottle and was told that's the way the coolers are and I would just need to put it back onto the machine before putting a new bottle on.

I contacted Sparkletts and DS Waters of America as well as Oasis International who actually makes the cooler and told them about the issue and the fact that he now have mold growing beneath his home in Los Angeles due to the water damage their product caused, they have repeatedly ignored the problem and stated that since the home was built in 1920 their floor was not worth anything and they were not responsible. 

He found out that Patriarch Partners owns Oasis International and when he contacted them to talk to someone, they told him that they did not know anyone he could talk to and said they were disconnecting the call, they proceeded and done just that. 

The water cooler that these companies have provided consumers are dangerous and should be taken off the market due to the flood potential of them and the ability to cause mold to be in homes as a result. What recourse of action can we take against these companies ? Ignoring the problem is not getting rid of the mold which we are being exposed to and our floor is now coming apart.

When the flood happened, we had to move a gas oven to dry the water.  It was discovered by the gas company.  The gas line was leaking causing gas to enter out home which was an explosion hazard.  Had the cooler not flooded our home, we would not have moved the oven.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and a potential explosion hazard due to a gas leak, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The following is being provided on behalf of the family of the three year old child referenced below, who may be contacted through their legal representatives: [REDACTED].

On Christmas Eve of 2010, a three year old boy was on the main level of his family's three story home.  The family's home was equipped with a Destiny Residential Elevator manufactured by National Wheel-O-Vator, which has since been acquired by ThyssenKrupp Access Corporation and/or ThyssenKrupp Manufacturing, LLC.  The boy became entrapped between the hoistway door and elevator accordion car door on the second floor of the family's home.  The elevator was subsequently called from the third floor while the boy was entrapped between these doors.  The boy was subsequently found by his mother crushed by the elevator.  The jaws of life were used to extract the child from the elevator.  Unfortunately he suffered an anoxic brain injury as a result of this accident.  His brain injury is catastrophic and permanent and he now requires life care assistance for all of his activities of daily life.  

Notably, this is not the first case of child entrapment between the hoistway door and elevator car door/gate.  This issue has been known to the elevator industry since the 1930s.  Many children have been seriously injured or killed in similar accidents.  There are technologically and economically feasible designs that eliminate this hazard completely.

These elevators remain on the market today.  There has been no effort to date to notify or warn current owners of Destiny Residential Elevators of the known hazard of child entrapment, which hazard can result in catastrophic injury or death. Earlier this year, ThyssenKrupp Access announced that it is ceasing its US operations at the end of 2012.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a three-year-old child, and similar incidents have occurred in the past, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The reporter stated that he was a door greater at a retailer and he noticed that there was a safety hazards with the carts used at the store. The reporter stated that these carts are the ones that the attached baby seat located on the rear of the shopping cart.

The reporter informed me that the baby seats located on the carts were supported by a stainless steel plate. The reporters stated that the cart was cracking and breaking on the spot weld that connects the stainless steel tube which was attached to a plate. The consumer stated that these stainless steel tubes and plates are only supported by these spot welds. 

The consumer stated he felt that it was a fall hazard for children who are placed on these baby seats, because the support of the seat can easily break.

The consumer believes that these seats can easily fall off the cart and he was afraid this could happen when a baby was inside the seat. 

The reporter stated that he informed management and they pulled all their carts from this particular store. Although he was afraid that corporate was not doing anything to inform other locations of the hazard that this carts can pose.

UPDATE:
Since I made the original report I have obtained more information pertinent to the failed baby mounted on the grocery carts used by Wal-Mart stores. The name of the seat is SAFE SEAT, manufactured by sse Inc. of Fairfield, NJ.

I also photographed the seats that failed at our store. Unfortunately some of the pictures are a little out of focus. When I took the pictures ,I was in bright sun and was unable to preview the photos after they were taken.

Picture one. The seat (a) is made with a foam material and is surrounded with a metal tube with a tube that goes down the back of the seat (b). This tube is attached wlith one spot weld (c) to a metal plated (d). The metal plate has a bracket that surrounds the metal tube (e) but that is not otherwise attached to the seat except for one spot weld at the other end of the plate. If the spot weld fails the seat is free to detach from the mounting plate.

Picture two. This shows a side view of a seat which has not totally failed.The spot weld has signs of a crack which probably means that this seat is about to fail.

Pictures three, four and five. These are pictures of three other seats where the weld has failed and the seat has become detached from the mounting plate.

Picture six. This photo shows a plate and bracket from one ofthe failed seats.

Picture seven. Shows a front view of the seat with the cracked spot weld. This seat in the normal position for use.

Picture eight. A side view showing the Manufactures logo .

Picture nine. Warning label on seat.

I also examined two more of theses seats at Wal-Mart's Union, Mo store but was unable to take photos. Both of these carts are newer that the ones at the Washington, Mo but both showed a thin line of rest across the spot weld which indicates that there are fine cracks in the weld.
justification: The incident involves a potential injury to children due to the failure of spot welds supporting baby seats on shopping carts, with multiple instances already reported.

incident_description:
Pride Mobility Lift Chair company makes lift chairs for the disabled and handicapped. Their power outage backup is so weak it only goes half way and leaves the individual stuck in the sitting position. It's made that way. Several very reasonable battery backups are available for $50. Pride's is made for 2 small  9 volt batteries and do not come with the chair. Many others are 550 volts and up and can be used for wireless phones and computers with 8 backup plugs. Besides they are rechargeable too. Prides are not and must be replaced frequently. The attitude of this company is to pass off any complaint without considering any action whatsoever. Pride chairs have been made this way for many years and they are stuck in the mud and refuse suggestions to help. They do not take any suggestions or complaints seriously and are putting their customers at risk. I recommend someone seriously look into this matter an see if you do not agree that the elderly, handicapped, disabled are not worth a better safety power backup system.

CONSUMER UPDATE: Pride Lift Chairs leave the handicapped person with unreasonable risk for injury or worse during times of power outages. Their battery backup system is inadequate and underpowered. My efforts to get Pride to seriously consider correcting this hazard goes without suggest. Pride lift chairs come with only a non rechargeable 2-9 volt battery backup system that does not lift the handicapped. It is made to only half work. That is to sit only not lift so a person can get out of the chair during power outages. It only moves from a reclining position to sitting. If the power goes out while sitting the system does not move.
There are several reasonable rechargeable battery systems costing $55 to $75 with 550 to 750 volts each that will lift the handicapped person from recline to sitting and standing. Prides system leaves one stranded while the others lift just like the chair is designed to do using public electric power.
This company is so arrogant they stop me from communicating with their management and do nothing to consider redesigning their chair for customer safety.
PrideÃÂs Chairman and CEO [REDACTED] is not allowed to see my letters and is not aware of the legal risk Pride is exposed. No others at Pride so far have made improvements for this chair for all the many years the tiny 9 volt backup. They have 50 Engineers and refuse to consider correcting this serious flaw.
justification: The inadequate power outage backup system can leave users, many of whom are elderly or disabled, stranded in a sitting position, posing a significant risk of injury.

incident_description: I am calling for the recall of the Kroger's kiddie race car cart. My daughter [REDACTED] was stuck in the basket for about 15mins on 07/08/2012. They had to take the basket apart with wrenches, pliers and screw drivers because from her knee to her foot was wedged in the small basket underneath the set.  If one moved her then extreme presser was on her knee, leg and ankle which  would have caused a brake of her knee, leg or ankle. After trying to get her unstuck for about 8mins, I demanded the fire department be called. The fire department arrived just as the managers pull the basket apart with all their might. They're our heroes. This happened at the Kroger [REDACTED].  The kiddie car cart doesn't feature a release on any of the sides of the cart if a child is stuck in the cart. My child is 3 and she weighs 34 pounds. I [REDACTED]attached some footage that one of the customers taped [REDACTED. They're still using the bashets
justification: Potential for serious injury (broken bones) was high due to the child's leg being wedged and the prolonged extraction process.

incident_description: While riding in the race cart shopping cart at BJ's, my daughter was reaching over the plastic portion that contains  the children's steering wheels and her fingers became trapped between the molded plastic and the wire basket. When I examined the cart after getting her loose, I noticed that the molded plastic curves upward at the sides, allowing for enough room to very easily get small fingers trapped between the plastic and basket.

The item said that it was approved for this age and weight. The strap goes over her head, over her shoulders, and between her legs to buckle. Thankfully I was right there and able to grab her quickly, but she turned herself around in the seat in an attempt to stand up. incident_description: Our building was remodeled in 2003 and approximately 43 emergency exit lights were installed. One year after occupation one of them caught fire-burning a mark approximately two feet or so up the wall then stopping. We thought it was an anomaly so did not address it other than to replace it. One had melted part of the lettering in the "exit" sign. The other showed the beginning of overheating with black burn marks on the wiring harness. We found these two during our bi-yearly battery testing of all units in the college in July of this year.
justification: Multiple instances of fire in emergency exit lights, with potential for escalation.

incident_description:
On Monday Morning July 25, 2011 around 10:20 am, my 2 year old daughter was at home when she burned her hand.  My daughter was able to draw water despite the alleged child resistant safety-spigot.  Her hand was scalded by the 175 degree water.  She suffered third degree burns on her hand. 

Ice Mountain Direct's home delivery website advertises that the hot water safety-spigot is child resistant, but our daughter was able to draw water despite the alleged  safety-spigot and dispense the water and burn her hand.  We received no instructions or warnings about the water cooler or the unsafe hot water valve or that the hot water feature could be physically turned off.

We believe Water Solutions/MTN Products manufactured the cooler.  We believe the spigot is manufactured by Tomlinson.  A disclaimer reads "Safety lock feature is no more than a deterrence to help prevent accidental use.  Children are inquisitive and will eventually figure out how to work this faucet, therefore should be used on cold and room temperature only."
justification: The incident resulted in third-degree burns, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the product's design and lack of adequate warnings.

incident_description:
I purchased this model 2-3 years ago from Lowe's.  This morning water started pouring out of the cooler from the inside and running out on the floor.  I could hear the heating element and cooling compressor running as my 5 year old stood in the water puddle and pointing out the cooler was leaking.  Unplugged it and move it outside.  I checked the LoweÃÂs reviews and noticed there were 16 out of 35 (46%) reviews that mentioned leaking.

It took a while to figure out what broke.  The hot water tank is mounted to the bottom of the main water reservoir.  The top threaded portion of the hot water tank is sealed to the bottom of the cold water reservoir with a compression fitting.  When the nut inside the reservoir is tightened, it pulls the hot water tank up and compresses the seals.   The threaded stem of the hot water tank sheared off just above the seals causing all of the water to stream out through the inside soaking the power cables.  I donÃÂt know what caused the other leaks mentioned in the reviews. 

The poor design of the tank compression fitting could lead to electrocution.
justification: Potential for severe injury, such as electrocution, due to poor design of the water tank compression fitting.

incident_description:
Crystal Springs 6750 Discovery Blvd. Mableton, Ga. 30126
Distributor: DS Waters of America Inc., of Atlanta, Ga.
       When installing a 5 gallon water bottle on the supplied  water cooler there was no warning label. To release anti drip requires pushing down on a bottle that weighs 44 pounds. The container did not have a handle to assist in the install. The snap release required an addition push of 26 pounds to release plastic cap. This allowed injury to right middle finger when it was wedged at base of water bottle. Doctor X-ray finger determined it had a fracture and was unable to work on that day.  This is a hazard that could have been avoided with proper warning sticker.   Also the release cap required additional pressure to install bottle pushing the bottle down with 70 pounds. I believe the safety release was defective and required the bottle to be pushed on to the cooler.
justification: Injury occurred due to lack of warning label and excessive force required to install the bottle, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I work as a Fire Marshal for the State of Vermont. An electrician had installed new exit/emergency light combonation signage. We did the initial test on them and they worked fine.
 We went back a week later and I tested them again, and some of the LED's didn't work so I told the electricain to check to see if the batteries and lights were ok.
The electrician then told us he turned off the power to work on another part of the lighting circuit and the exit/emergency lights were on for approx 30-45 minutes. He then said he smelled something burning and investigated and found the emergency light heads had burnt and started to melt. This happened on 4 of the 5 devices installed.

In another incident an electrician in another location installed the same type of device and when the lights were on for about 20 minutes and saw that the board inside the lights started to smoke.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, with four out of five devices burning and melting.

incident_description: We smelled a burning plastic smell and discovered it was our water jug cooler (dispenses hot and cold water). We unplugged it and took the back metal cover off to find a melted wire and black burn marks.
justification: No injuries were reported, but there was a significant incident involving a faulty electrical appliance.

We managed to get the entire costume and then found this portable smoke machine on amazon.  Once we charged the unit like the directions said to, we put it together and turned it on to test before using.  Within a few minutes, the unit started on fire and we had to put it out.  We notified the vendor and so far,  they have been not at all helpful with the fire that occured with their product.

incident_description: I want to report on Tatung Water Boiler/Water dispenser that my husband and I used to prepare formula for our 9-month-old baby. We would usually press the "boil" button and it heats up the hot water, and you press the "dispense" button and hot water will be dispensed from it. a week ago the dispense button stopped working, so we would manually scoop out the hot water with a ladle. yesterday night, the water boiler started reboiling multiple times through the night and it was all burnt up inside when I woke up from a terrible fume smell. I immediately unplugged it in case it caused any fire hazard.
justification: The water boiler's malfunction and continuous reboiling could have led to a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We have a home elevator Made by Residential Elevators.  I think it was installed in 2016 or 2017.  The doors are not compliant with the 3/4", 4" rules for safety to avoid child entrapment.  Many other vendors have addressed this risk with recalls and door baffle installation.  I just got a notice from Residential Elevator saying we must separately arrange for baffling and they won't do any maintenance for us until we do (https://residentialelevators.com/safety).  This seems ridiculous to me.  You seem to be letting this manufacturer shed responsibility for a known defect to the consumer while other manufacturers are convinced to accept the need for a safety recall.  These systems are all virtually identical in this respect.  Over 4 inches is over 4 inches.  Can you get Residential Elevators to recall their product and provide baffles?   I tried to get them on-line but they are constantly out of stock.  This is a known risk with a clear and straight forward correction that is only being partially implemented.
justification: No incident has occurred, but the non-compliant elevator doors pose a potential risk of child entrapment.

incident_description:
On February 1, 2017, a two and a half year old child was crushed under the car of a residential elevator.  The child died from his injuries.

This report is being filed by counsel for the deceased child's parents.  The filer previously notified the CPSC of potentially fatal hazards associated with many residential or home elevators and subsequently filed a "Petition For Recall to Repair/Retrofit and Rulemaking" (CP 15-1) with the CPSC on November 13, 2014.

The specific reason why and how the child wound up under the elevator car is not yet determined. An inspection of the elevator will take place on March 24, 2017 with multiple parties.
justification: The incident resulted in a fatality, and while the exact cause is not yet determined, the likelihood of such an event occurring is possible given the known hazards of residential elevators.

Same day, the consumer called the mfr's Recall # (800) 361-2836. and has called them every business day since that time.  No one has returned the consumer's call even though the people she spoke to said that they would.  

5/7/2016:  The consumer called the retailer:  810-985-4457 and she spoke to a rep., who informed her that they no longer sold this mfr's brand of stair lifts.


The consumer does not want risk being injured by this lift.
